definitions.reported: filed by the company for exactly that period
definitions.derived: a difference of two filed cumulative figures

quality.basis: trailing twelve months: the same four consecutive quarters for every line

rows.label: Free cash flow margin
rows.note: operating cash flow minus capital spending on property and equipment; capitalised software is not subtracted

rows.label: Cash conversion (operating cash flow / net income)
rows.note: not meaningful: the denominator is zero or negative

rows.label: Stock-based compensation / revenue
rows.note: an input is missing from the filings

rows.label: Operating income / invested capital (pre-tax)
rows.note: not meaningful: the denominator is zero or negative

balance.note: debt here is the long-term debt line the company tags; leases and short-term borrowings may be excluded, so it can understate what is owed

rule_of_40.definition: Rule of 40 (FCF basis) = TTM revenue growth % + TTM free-cash-flow margin %
rule_of_40.caveat: Reaching 40 does not mean a stock is undervalued, and missing it does not disqualify a company. Working-capital timing (for example annual upfront billing), stock-based compensation (not subtracted from free cash flow), acquisitions and unusual cash flows can move the score; check them in the filings.
rule_of_40.label: Below 40

ebitda_variant.label: Rule of 40 (EBITDA basis): a separate measure, not the default
ebitda_variant.reason: operating income or depreciation and amortisation is missing for these four quarters

peers.reason: Peer comparison needs the filings of comparable companies; add them to the comparison to see their scores side by side.

valuation.caveat: A model-dependent estimate under stated assumptions: not a forecast, price target or advice. Different reasonable assumptions give different answers.

multiples.label: EV / EBITDA
multiples.basis: enterprise value / TTM EBITDA (operating income + depreciation and amortisation)
multiples.note: not meaningful: EBITDA is missing or not positive

multiples.label: P/E
multiples.note: not meaningful: earnings are missing or not positive

multiples.label: Free-cash-flow yield (%)
multiples.basis: TTM free cash flow / market value x 100

inputs.shares_basis: weighted-average diluted shares for the year ended 2025-12-31

what_must_be_true: Rule of 40 (FCF basis) is 30.0 (60.0% growth + -30.0% free-cash-flow margin); a falling score would weaken the case.
what_would_disprove_it: Diluted share count rose 5.0% (2024-12-31 to 2025-12-31): continued dilution erodes per-share value even when revenue grows.
research_next: Open the latest annual report and read the segment, geography and customer-concentration notes (not in structured data).
Find recurring-revenue, retention and backlog disclosures, and separate organic growth from acquisitions and currency effects.
Check stock-based compensation and any acquisitions or one-off cash flows inside the trailing twelve months.
